findings.message: This fixes only the status, not its consumers. `githubAppStatus` now returns `usable: null` and `checkProblem`, but it still sets `configured: true` when the check couldn't run. Two consumers still read that as configured. First, `admin(set)` in chat-suggestions.ts compares only `.configured === set`, so chat keeps offering Rotate and Remove as if the value had been checked. Second, the Integrations chip (apps/web/app/(app)/settings/integrations/page.tsx:38) still shows the green `good` chip reading "Configured · couldn't check it". The previous finding asked for both consumers to show 'couldn't check' instead of Configured, and not to offer Rotate or Remove. Fix: when `usable === null`, the suggestions offer neither Set up nor Rotate/Remove (or a 'check again' prompt), and the chip shows a neutral "Couldn't check" state without the `good` class.
findings.scenario: An incomplete value is stored, then the KMS goes down. An Admin opens /settings/integrations and sees a green chip, "Configured · couldn't check it". Chat offers ["Rotate the GitHub app secret", "Remove the GitHub app"] when it should offer neither, and it doesn't offer Set up, which the stored value actually needs.

findings.message: The table still has no row for a refused use (ForbiddenError or another non-refusal useSecret error), although the previous finding named that variant. Those errors take the generic branch in `problemOf`, and no test covers that branch. The second row's `why` is `/./`, which any non-empty string matches, so that row's reason check proves nothing. The test also never checks `offered()` during the outage, which is why the folded-to-configured suggestions above go unnoticed. Fix: add a refused-use row and a row for an unexpected error, each with a specific expected reason. Assert `offered()` during the outage as well. Restore the KMS in a `finally` so a throwing `status()` can't leak the outage config into later tests.
findings.scenario: Make `problemOf` throw or return '' for non-ToolError errors, or reintroduce Rotate/Remove for an unchecked status. Every row of the table stays green.

findings.message: The new guard comment says "a late failure never drops a newer check" (the `checks.get(...)?.answer === answer` comparison), but no test runs a failing read that overlaps a newer check. Deleting the comparison leaves every test green. The only effect is one extra audited read, so this is minor. Add an overlapping-check test or drop the claim.
findings.scenario: Check A fails after a rotation has already started check B. Without the guard, A's catch deletes B's entry. No test fails.
